sections.h2: Where in Wilmington do you take a deed to be recorded?
sections.html:
Real estate recording for New Hanover County is handled in Land Records, Suite 102, at 320 Chestnut Street in Wilmington. A second counter on Government Center Drive takes recordings in the afternoon only.

  • Land Records, Suite 102 (main office), 320 Chestnut Street, Wilmington, NC 28401: Monday through Friday, 8 to 5.
  • Vital Services, Suite 120 (same building): Monday through Friday, 8 to 5.
  • Satellite office, 230 Government Center Drive, Wilmington, NC 28403: recording from 2 pm to 5 pm on weekdays, vital records from 8 am to 5 pm.

Per the county's Register of Deeds page, the office number is 910-798-4530, and anything sent by mail must go to the Suite 102 address, never the satellite site.

sections.h2: What information does New Hanover County want on page one?
sections.html:
Quite a bit. Beyond the statewide format rules, the county requires the following on its recordings:

  • A return name and address for the original document.
  • The drafter's name, on every deed and deed of trust.
  • The parcel's tax ID number, on any document that conveys land.
  • The grantee's address, again on conveyances of land.

Tax ID numbers come from Land Records in the county Tax Department, at 910-798-7300. Pull the number early, since it has to be typed onto the deed before anyone signs.

sections.h2: How does the county treat paper that is not standard?
sections.html:
New Hanover County will still record it, for an extra $25.00 under G.S. 161-10(a)(19) on top of ordinary fees. Follow the county's own list below when you file in Wilmington.

  • Page sizes: 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • Margins: three inches blank at the top of page one, half an inch elsewhere on that page, and half an inch on every side of later pages.
  • Ink and font: black on white, with 9 points counted as the smallest legible size.
  • Sides: text on the front of the sheet only.
  • Label: the instrument type at the top of page one, outside the blank margin.

Blanks may be inked in by hand, and fixes must use black ink. Releases of deeds of trust or mortgages, in every form, and UCC filings do not have to meet these standards.

sections.h2: What does the county charge to record and copy real estate documents?
sections.html:
The fee schedule for fiscal year 2026-27, revised July 1, 2026, lists the charges below. Plats and maps have their own lines, and a deed that must be re-indexed under later instruments can draw extra index fees.

Real estate filing and copy fees, New Hanover County Fee Schedule FY26-27, Register of Deeds section

Deed or other instrument, up to 15 pages$26, plus $4 for each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage, up to 35 pages$64, plus $4 for each added page
Each multiple instrument$10 additional

Source: New Hanover County Fee Schedule. The same schedule charges $10 for a notary oath and $5 for a notarial act.

sections.h2: What does the county say about excise stamps?
sections.html:
The county prints the rate as $1.00 per $500.00 of price, which it says works out to $2.00 per $1,000.00, and it adds that state law makes the seller pay. G.S. 105-228.30 requires payment at the register before recording.

A caller who asks what a house sold for will be told only the stamp amount. The Register does not search titles or report on liens.

The county's fee schedule also prints the stamp rate by era: $2 per $1,000 from 1991 to the present, $1 per $1,000 from 1968 to 1991, and $1.10 per $1,000 before 1968. That history matters if you read an old deed and wonder what its stamp meant.

sections.h2: What can the New Hanover County register do, and what is off limits?
sections.html:
The office keeps the public record and does not advise. The county's FAQ draws the lines clearly.

  • Off limits: legal advice, attorney referrals and title searches.
  • Public: every filed record except DD-214 discharges, open to viewing and copying at the office.
  • Name changes on title: a new deed is needed to add or drop a name.
  • Wills: filed with the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Maps: subdivision and condominium plats only, not lot surveys.
  • House size and age: ask the Tax Department.

There is also a free fraud alert. Once you enroll, any document recorded under your name triggers an email with a copy. Owners of a vacant or inherited house may find that worth setting up.

sections.h2: Why does the order of recording matter in New Hanover County?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, whichever instrument is registered first takes priority, and a deed that was never registered gives no protection against lien creditors or buyers who paid value. A deed signed on Friday but filed the following week can lose to something registered in between.

Because the office does not run title searches, ask an attorney or title company to check for open liens before anything is signed.

sections.h2: What other services does the Wilmington office run?
sections.html:
Besides land records, the staff issue certified vital records, passport services and military discharge filings, and they take e-filed assumed business name certificates. Marriage licenses need an appointment, while notary oaths do not.

The county's page also links a public records search and a guide called "Don't Overpay for a Copy of Your House Deed," useful when a closing needs a copy of the vesting deed. The fee schedule lists first-time adult passport books at $165 and passport cards at $65, and certified birth, death and marriage copies at $10 each. A marriage license is $60, and a minor's passport book is $135. Mailed requests for uncertified vital record copies carry a $1.25 fee on the same schedule. For a business-name form, the office keeps printed copies of the Secretary of State form as a courtesy.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about New Hanover housing?
sections.html:
New Hanover County has 128,402 housing units, with 104,856 households averaging 2.19 people. Owners live in 61.4% of occupied homes, which leaves nearly 39% for renters paying a median of $1,417 a month.

Residents who stayed in the same house for a full year make up 83.8%, and 45.4% of adults aged 25 or older finished a bachelor's degree. The county saw 2,332 building permits in 2025. For a seller, the lesson from the recording rules is to arrive with a deed showing the drafter, tax ID and grantee address on page one.

faqs.q: What is the street address for recording a deed in Wilmington?
faqs.a: Go to 320 Chestnut Street, Suite 102, in Wilmington (ZIP 28401). A satellite counter at 230 Government Center Drive takes recordings from 2 pm to 5 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: Will New Hanover County accept a deed by mail?
faqs.a: Yes, but only to the Suite 102 address on Chestnut Street. The county says mailed recordings should not go to the satellite office.

faqs.q: Who owes the New Hanover County excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. The county prints the rate as $1.00 per $500.00, and the register can later tell you only the stamp amount on the recorded deed.

faqs.q: Where can I find my parcel's tax ID for a New Hanover County deed?
faqs.a: Ask Land Records at the county Tax Department, 910-798-7300. The number belongs on page one next to the grantee's address.

faqs.q: Are wills filed with the New Hanover County register?
faqs.a: No. They go to the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court. The register handles deeds and other property records.
